fields.headline: PARAVISION WINS UP TO $6.5M STATE CONTRACT
fields.deck: The firm-fixed-price award was made September 23 and covers digital identity assurance.

stories.caption:
The State Department has given facial recognition developer Paravision a contract worth up to $6.5 million. Federal procurement records describe the work as digital detection and identity assurance.

The award was made September 23 with $1.3 million obligated at the start. The firm-fixed-price contract can run through September 22, 2031. The department competed it under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and Paravision was the only offeror.

Public award records do not name the Paravision products bought. The description overlaps with the company's deepfake detection and liveness technology, which it markets to guard digital identity systems against manipulated and AI-generated faces. The records do not show whether those products are part of the award. Paravision also received a separate $24,717 purchase order from the department on April 30 for a purchase card tied to a software license, and public records do not say whether that was a test or a precursor to the September contract.

Source: Biometric Update, 17OCT26

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

fields.headline: XTEND BOOKS 6,000 STRIKER DRONE ORDER
fields.deck: The $40.5M order follows a top Close Quarters Battle result in Gauntlet II.

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics (NYSE: XTND) has received a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER systems. The order comes after the company was named a top performer in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II in the U.S. Drone Dominance Program, which the Department of War runs as an iterative $1 billion effort.

STRIKER is built on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is aimed at tactical missions in confined, complex and GNSS-denied environments. CEO Aviv Shapira said the order reflects trust in the company's technology and its ability to deliver at scale, adding, "We competed, we proved our capabilities, and now we are ready to build."

Gauntlet II top performers advance directly to Gauntlet III in their selected mission set, but only after first fulfilling a 400-system production order. The company says Gauntlet III results will determine whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and that participation does not guarantee an award.

The release also gave preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue and a backlog update.

Source: XTEND AI Robotics via Business Wire, 13OCT26

fields.deck: The Army plans to deliver tested solutions to Soldiers within 180 days.

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is working with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to test emerging systems in Africa and get them to Soldiers within 180 days.

The command's first accelerated capability event, known as an ACE, is planned for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It will center on counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, aimed at shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. The Army says Africa's open spectrum, lightly used airspace and varied terrain let Soldiers validate solutions in theater before scaling them across the service.

Per the Army, SETAF-AF will run a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027 in Tan-Tan, with a later operational assessment during the April and May 2027 iteration of African Lion. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

fields.headline: OSC OFFERS ANTHEIA UP TO $80M LOAN
fields.deck: The conditional loan would support Antheia's U.S. drug ingredient manufacturing.

stories.caption:
The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital has issued a conditional commitment to Antheia, a biosynthesis company based in Menlo Park, Calif., for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million. The company says the financing, alongside additional private capital, would support its U.S. manufacturing strategy for critical pharmaceutical ingredients.

Roughly nine in ten of the key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients the country depends on come from abroad, a dependence Antheia describes as leaving Americans exposed to drug shortages. Antheia says it has previously received $32 million in non-dilutive federal financing and equity from strategic government-affiliated investors.

Dr. Christina Smolke, Antheia's CEO and co-founder, called reliance on foreign suppliers for these ingredients an ongoing public health and national security risk. The commitment is not final. The loan specifies further steps Antheia must complete before financial close, including financial, legal, technical, investment and due diligence requirements.

Source: PR Newswire, Oct. 18, 2026

fields.headline: TOP DEFENSE DEVELOPMENTS
fields.story_03: Florida Guard tests drones at Blanding

stories.caption:
MilCityUSA's ICYMI brief covers three stories published last week. Each one is listed above and appears in full in the posts that follow.

Microchip Technology acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and its HARDSIL process technology to Microchip's space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge as its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard ran Drone Crucible 26.3, an integration test at Camp Blanding from Sept. 26 to Oct. 2, that connected drone, tactical and command information into a shared picture.

Source: MilCityUSA ICYMI, 18OCT26.
